content:
# S3 Logs Bucket with ACK

Below are the new manifests to add to your `dev/` and `prod/` directories. Each directory gets an independent logs bucket and permission grant.

**Key notes:**
- Adjust `userName: myapp-user` (dev) and `roleName: myapp-role` (prod) if your existing User/Role have different names
- The `Policy` resources create AWS-managed policies; `UserPolicyAttachment` and `RolePolicyAttachment` attach them to the existing principals
- Each environment is fully isolated; changes in one directory do not affect the other

---

`dev/logs-bucket.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-dev
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-dev
  versioningConfiguration:
    status: Enabled
  serverSideEncryptionConfiguration:
    rules:
    - applyServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
        sseAlgorithm: AES256
  publicAccessBlockConfiguration:
    blockPublicAcls: true
    ignorePublicAcls: true
    blockPublicPolicy: true
    restrictPublicBuckets: true
```

`dev/logs-policy.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-policy-dev
spec:
  policyName: myapp-logs-policy-dev
  policyDocument: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [
        {
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Action": [
            "s3:GetObject",
            "s3:PutObject"
          ],
          "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-dev/*"
        }
      ]
    }
---
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: UserPolicyAttachment
metadata:
  name: myapp-user-logs-dev
spec:
  userName: myapp-user
  policyName: myapp-logs-policy-dev
```

---

`prod/logs-bucket.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-prod
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-prod
  versioningConfiguration:
    status: Enabled
  serverSideEncryptionConfiguration:
    rules:
    - applyServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
        sseAlgorithm: AES256
  publicAccessBlockConfiguration:
    blockPublicAcls: true
    ignorePublicAcls: true
    blockPublicPolicy: true
    restrictPublicBuckets: true
```

`prod/logs-policy.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-policy-prod
spec:
  policyName: myapp-logs-policy-prod
  policyDocument: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [
        {
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Action": [
            "s3:GetObject",
            "s3:PutObject"
          ],
          "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-prod/*"
        }
      ]
    }
---
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: RolePolicyAttachment
metadata:
  name: myapp-role-logs-prod
spec:
  roleName: myapp-role
  policyName: myapp-logs-policy-prod
```

---

**To apply:**
```bash
kubectl apply -f dev/logs-bucket.yaml -f dev/logs-policy.yaml
kubectl apply -f prod/logs-bucket.yaml -f prod/logs-policy.yaml
```

**Alternative: inline policy edit**

If you prefer to edit the existing `iam.yaml` files instead of creating separate policy files, add an `inlinePolicies` field to your existing User (dev) and Role (prod) specs:

```yaml
# In dev/iam.yaml, add to the User spec:
inlinePolicies:
  logs-access: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [
        {
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Action": ["s3:GetObject", "s3:PutObject"],
          "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-dev/*"
        }
      ]
    }

# In prod/iam.yaml, add to the Role spec:
inlinePolicies:
  logs-access: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [
        {
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Action": ["s3:GetObject", "s3:PutObject"],
          "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-prod/*"
        }
      ]
    }
```

Either approach fulfills the requirement; separate policy files are cleaner for modularity, while inline policies keep all IAM configuration in one place.
